name: Islamic Services Foundation
mission: The Islamic Services Foundation (ISF) is a non-profit organization, which has been dedicated to serving the Muslim community since its founding in 1989. Heaquarted in the Dallas, Texas Area, ISF is home to serveral community service projects. Islamic Services Foundation is the parent company of Brighter Horizons Academy, Islamic Curriculum Project, Muslim Yellow Pages and Texas Islamic Court.

judge_issues.message: The charity's primary programs focus on education (Brighter Horizons Academy, financial aid for students) and community services. While 'Fi Sabilillah' (religious/educational causes) is a valid zakat category, the classification as 'riqab' (modern interpretation: human trafficking victims) is not supported by the provided program descriptions.

While the charity's primary focus is education, the 'Fi Sabilillah' category can encompass religious and educational causes. Explicitly linking educational programs to this asnaf would strengthen the classification.

rich_narrative.summary: founded in 1989, the Islamic Services Foundation (ISF) serves the Muslim community in North Texas through education and social services. The organization operates several key institutions, including <cite id="1">Brighter Horizons Academy and Little Horizons Academy</cite>. While the foundation maintains a long operational history, its financial profile shows recent shifts. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="6">total revenue of $12,484,881</cite>, which represents a <cite id="6">12% decline from the $14,235,728 reported in FY2023</cite>. Despite this revenue dip, ISF maintains a <cite id="4">program expense ratio of 99.5%</cite>, indicating that all reported expenses are directed toward its core missions. The organization is <cite id="5">recognized as zakat-eligible</cite>, focusing its aid on categories such as the poor (fuqara) and needy (masakin). Beyond its primary K-12 educational focus, ISF manages the <cite id="1">ISF Qur’an Institute and provides halal certification services</cite>. Its educational impact is measurable, with a <cite id="1">graduating class of 72 students</cite> and the distribution of <cite id="1">$1,000,000 in financial aid</cite> to support its student body. However, the high cost of its intensive educational model results in a <cite id="4">cost per beneficiary exceeding $13,220</cite>, which is a significant investment per individual served.
